ambiguities.description: The final exchange raises whether a grade can be recorded for a student who is enrolled but whose enrollment is not yet finalized, or whether the grade is always tied strictly to enrollment. The phrase 'were enrolled' (past tense) versus 'enrolled in' distinction is not explored -- e.g., can a student receive a grade if they later withdrew, or is the grade only for currently-enrolled students? This affects whether the subset constraint linking grades to enrollment is exact or approximate.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. The grade is one of A, B, C, D, or F. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: It is not stated whether every enrolled student is guaranteed to eventually receive a grade (mandatory in the other direction) -- only that at most one grade per offering is given, leaving open whether a grade is mandatory for every enrollment or optional (e.g., incomplete/no grade cases).

source_references.excerpt: A student gets at most one grade per offering.
